topic.title: Ritlecitinib for Alopecia Areata in Patients Under 18 Years of Age: A Single-Center Retrospective Real-World Study
topic.abstract: Purpose: Alopecia areata (AA) in pediatric and adolescent patients can be severe and difficult to manage, and real-world data on targeted therapies in this population remain limited. Ritlecitinib, a selective JAK3/TEC inhibitor, has demonstrated efficacy in adults with AA, but evidence in patients under 18 years of age is scarce. The purpose of this study is to assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of ritlecitinib in pediatric and adolescent patients with alopecia areata. Patients and methods: This retrospective real-world study included patients aged <18 years with AA treated with ritlecitinib 50 mg once daily. Treatment response was assessed using changes in Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) scores and achievement of SALT50/75/90 at the last on-treatment observation. Safety outcomes were evaluated based on clinical records. Results: Twenty-seven patients were included, with a median age of 9.3 years (IQR, 6.0-14.6), including patients younger than 12 years who received off-label treatment. The median baseline SALT score was 50. The median SALT score decreased to 0 at the last observation (p < 0.001). SALT50, SALT75, and SALT90 were achieved by 96.3%, 77.8%, and 55.6% of patients, respectively, and 51.9% achieved complete scalp regrowth. Treatment responses were observed in both patchy AA and AT/AU subgroups; however, interpretation of subgroup differences is limited by the small sample sizes. No serious adverse events or treatment discontinuations due to adverse events were documented in the available medical records. Conclusion: In this single-center retrospective cohort, ritlecitinib treatment was associated with substantial improvement in SALT scores and no documented serious adverse events during the observation period. These preliminary findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies, particularly in children younger than 12 years receiving off-label treatment.

sections.label: 배경
sections.title: Introduction
sentences: Signaling downstream of cytokines such as interleukin-15 and interferon-γ plays a key role in sustaining immune-mediated damage to the hair follicle.1

Ritlecitinib has been investigated in randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trials and long-term open-label studies, demonstrating clinically meaningful hair regrowth and an acceptable safety profile in adolescents and adults with moderate-to-severe AA.2 In June 2023, ritlecitinib received regulatory approval in the United States for the treatment of severe AA in patients aged 12 years and older, expanding the therapeutic landscape for patients with limited options.

Despite this progress, there remains a need for real-world evidence to characterize the effectiveness and tolerability of ritlecitinib in routine clinical practice, particularly in younger populations who may exhibit unique disease dynamics or treatment responses.3 Although ritlecitinib has demonstrated efficacy in adolescents and adults with AA, real-world evidence in younger pediatric populations, particularly children younger than 12 years receiving off-label treatment, remains limited.

sections.label: 연구 방법
sections.title: Materials and Methods
sentences: Patients treated between January 2024 and August 2025 were retrospectively screened for eligibility.

Patients were eligible for inclusion if they met all of the following criteria: (1) age younger than 18 years at the time of ritlecitinib initiation; (2) a clinical diagnosis of alopecia areata, including patchy alopecia areata, alopecia totalis, or alopecia universalis, established by experienced dermatologists based on clinical presentation; (3) treatment with oral ritlecitinib 50 mg once daily in routine clinical practice; (4) available baseline SALT score before treatment initiation; and (5) at least one documented on-treatment follow-up assessment of scalp hair loss severity.
Secondary effectiveness outcomes included the proportion of patients achieving SALT50, SALT75, and SALT90, defined as ≥50%, ≥75%, and ≥90% improvement from baseline SALT score, respectively.

sections.label: 고찰
sections.title: Discussion
sentences: In this real-world cohort of pediatric and adolescent patients with alopecia areata, ritlecitinib treatment was associated with substantial scalp hair regrowth, and no serious adverse events were documented during the available observation period.

Marked reductions in SALT scores were observed from baseline to the last on-treatment assessment, with most patients achieving clinically meaningful response thresholds, including SALT50, SALT75, and SALT ≤20.
Notably, more than half of the cohort achieved complete scalp regrowth, suggesting potential clinical benefit in this cohort.
Larger prospective controlled studies with standardized follow-up are needed to confirm its effectiveness and safety, particularly among children younger than 12 years receiving off-label treatment.
